newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Eletrobras won't sell small power units separately.
newsitem.headline: Eletrobras won't sell small power units separately.

text.p: Brazil's National Privatization Council (CND) has decided that Eletrobras's small power plants should be sold together with its large subsidiaries, a BNDES spokesman said.

"The council has decided to include Eletrobras's small hydroelectric and thermoelectric plants in the privatization of its large subsidiaries," said a spokesman for the National Development Bank (BNDES), who asked not to be named.

This decision has blocked Eletrobras plans, announced late last year, to auction off its small power plants in the first half of 1997 separately from its large units. The company had planned to raise 3 billion reais with the sale of its small power plants.

Eletrobras has four large subsidiaries, Furnas, Eletrosul, Eletronorte and Chesf, whose privatization is expected to start late this year as soon as British consulting firm Coopers & Lybrand finishes pricing Eletrobras assets, he said.
